claim: Singapore's Ministerial Committee on Ageing released the full Action Plan for Successful Ageing report on 24 February 2016, with the government committing S$3 billion to implement it; the plan details more than 70 initiatives to empower Singaporeans to age confidently, and the report was launched by Senior Minister of State for Health Amy Khor.
source_note: Found via search for the National Innovation Challenge on Active and Confident Ageing, which surfaced this MOH newsroom press release. The Action Plan was first announced in 2015; this release marks the publication of the full report.

claim: On 30 January 2023 Singapore's Ministerial Committee on Ageing launched the refreshed 2023 Action Plan for Successful Ageing, anchored on three pillars — Care, Contribution and Connectedness — focusing on community initiatives to empower Singaporeans to take charge of their own ageing journeys.
source_note: Found via search for the 2023 refresh of the Action Plan for Successful Ageing; MOH newsroom press release. The full plan PDF is also on moh.gov.sg (refreshed-action-plan-for-successful-ageing-2023.pdf).

claim: On 16 November 2023 the Singapore Ministries of Health, National Development and Transport jointly announced Age Well SG, a national programme to support seniors to age well in their homes and communities, with MOH dedicating around S$800 million from FY2024 to FY2028 to better resource Active Ageing Centres.
source_note: Found via search for the Age Well SG announcement; MOH newsroom press release, mirrored on mot.gov.sg.

claim: In his National Day Rally speech on 20 August 2023, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said Singapore is an aged society that will soon be a 'super-aged' society, and announced a new national programme, Age Well SG, to complement Healthier SG in improving the health of seniors.
source_note: Full speech transcript on the PMO website, found via search for the Age Well SG rally announcement.

claim: In a 12 October 2024 progress update on Age Well SG, the Singapore government stated it has set aside S$3.5 billion over the next decade for the programme, and will dedicate a further S$140 million from FY2025 to FY2027 for infrastructural upgrades of existing Active Ageing Centres.
source_note: MOH newsroom press release found via search for Age Well SG funding. The S$3.5 billion figure was originally announced at Budget 2024, but the MOF budget statement PDF could not be text-extracted, so this dated MOH release is the working source for the figure.

claim: Speaking at the 3rd Centre for Research on Successful Ageing Symposium on 12 October 2023, Health Minister Ong Ye Kung said Singapore's average lifespan is about 84 years while average health span is 74 years, meaning the average Singaporean suffers ten years of ill health before passing away.
source_note: MOH newsroom speech transcript, found via search for Ong Ye Kung healthspan speeches.

claim: At the Business Times Longevity Forum on 25 July 2026, Health Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies Ong Ye Kung said the real KPI for healthcare today is the gap between healthspan and lifespan — about 11 to 12 years in developed economies — and that squeezing it down to below 10 years would make life much better.
source_note: MOH newsroom speech transcript, found via search for Ong Ye Kung longevity speeches.

claim: At the National Medical Research Council Awards Ceremony on 22 May 2026, Health Minister Ong Ye Kung said the government has committed S$350 million under RIE2030 for the RIE Grand Challenge on Maximising Healthy and Successful Longevity, supporting research areas including brain health (vascular dementia), physical function (sarcopenic obesity and frailty) and socio-environmental support for healthy longevity.
source_note: MOH newsroom speech transcript, found via search for Ong Ye Kung longevity speeches. See sg-009 for the RIE2030 plan itself.

claim: On 5 December 2025 Singapore unveiled the S$37 billion RIE2030 research plan (about 1% of GDP over five years from April 2026). Its first RIE Grand Challenge, Maximising Healthy and Successful Longevity, addresses the rapid transition to a super-aged society by increasing understanding of the biology of ageing in the population and the ability to intervene early and effectively.
source_note: Official National Research Foundation (Prime Minister's Office) press release PDF on the government file service file.go.gov.sg; the nrf.gov.sg copy of the PDF returned 404 at retrieval time. Dateline 'Singapore, 5 December 2025'; the plan was endorsed at the 15th RIEC meeting that day. Quotes verified against the PDF text.

claim: In October 2021 the Housing & Development Board, the National University of Singapore and the National University Health System announced plans for the pilot Health District @ Queenstown, a first-of-its-kind multi-stakeholder collaboration whose stated aims include promoting healthy longevity by increasing residents' health span.
source_note: Found via search for Health District @ Queenstown. Publisher is NUS News (an institutional primary partner), not a .gov.sg site — the HDB page on the Health District returned 404 at retrieval time, hence medium confidence; the content itself is directly supported. The plans were announced by Minister Desmond Lee at the HDB Awards ceremony.

claim: In his Committee of Supply speech on 3 March 2026, Manpower Minister Tan See Leng announced that Singapore will raise the statutory retirement and re-employment ages to 64 and 69 respectively on 1 July 2026, keeping the country on track to raise them to 65 and 70 by 2030, framing the move around Singaporeans leading longer, healthier lives and 'career longevity'.
source_note: MOM newsroom speech, found via search restricted to mom.gov.sg. Classified as legislation because it concerns the statutory ages under the Retirement and Re-employment Act; the gazetted notifications on sso.agc.gov.sg returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval, so the announcing speech is the working source — hence medium confidence on the classification. MOM's employment-practices retirement page (updated 1 July 2026) corroborates the minimum retirement age of 64.

claim: In a written parliamentary reply of 5 July 2021 to Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Singapore's Minister for Health described the whole-of-government approach to ageing coordinated by the Ministerial Committee on Ageing, including the 2015 Action Plan for Successful Ageing, and stated the MCA would refresh the Action Plan to keep catering to the evolving needs of current and future seniors.
source_note: MOH newsroom parliamentary QA, found via search for MOH parliamentary replies on ageing. The reply is dated 5 July 2021; the page footer carries a later 'last updated' stamp.

claim: In a parliamentary reply published 10 September 2024 to Nominated MP Neil Parekh, Singapore's Minister for Health stated that reducing the current ten-year gap between health-span and life-span is the ultimate objective of healthcare, and pointed to employers' role via continued employment of older workers and workplace health practices aligned with Healthier SG.
source_note: MOH newsroom parliamentary QA, found via search for MOH parliamentary replies on the healthspan-lifespan gap. Sitting date 9 September 2024, page publication date 10 September 2024 (used as source_date).

claim: In his Ministry of Health Committee of Supply speech on 6 March 2024, Health Minister Ong Ye Kung said a person in Singapore is expected to live to 74 in good health — one of the highest healthspans in the world — and that with the number of Singaporean seniors up almost 20% in five years to 690,000, Singapore is on the verge of being a super-aged society, with interventions continuing to roll out through Age Well SG.
source_note: MOH newsroom speech transcript, found via search for Ong Ye Kung healthspan speeches. This speech does not itself state the Age Well SG dollar figures (those are in sg-003 and sg-005).
